founder: Jeff Berg and Aaron Stewart (co-founders; Jeff Spillman joined early as operations/culture lead)

category: Vertical SaaS / Church management (worship planning + full ChMS suite)

customerSegment: SMB-to-enterprise churches; US plus Canada, Australia, NZ (localized giving rates).
coreProblem: Planning Sunday services and running church operations meant spreadsheets, Access databases, retyped orders of service, and chaotic volunteer coordination.

problemSeverity: HIGH for staff time/stress; MEDIUM-HIGH business pain (errors visible to whole congregation).
existingAlternatives: Spreadsheets, Access/FileMaker databases, Shelby, Fellowship One, ACS/Realm, paper planning-center binders.
currentUserWorkflow: Staff updated 3+ Excel sheets plus Access plus website weekly; burned CDs/uploaded MP3s for musicians; phoned volunteers to confirm serving slots.
productSolution: Modular suite (Services, People, Check-Ins, Giving, Groups, Registrations, Calendar, Publishing) plus free Church Center congregant app.
coreFeature: Service planning with drag-and-drop order of service, auto-timing and one-click volunteer accept/decline scheduling.
initialMVP: Drag-and-drop order of service with timing, built for their own church; then the accept/decline volunteer button that 'changed everything.'
featuresNotInMVP: Giving, Check-Ins, Registrations, Calendar, Church Center app, Publishing; founders explicitly said 'We will never be a church management system.'
currentFeatureSet: 8+ products: People, Services, Music Stand, Check-Ins, Giving, Groups, Registrations, Calendar, Publishing, Church Center app, PicoLabs experiments.
pricingModel: Modular per-product subscriptions scaled by usage; no contracts; giving processing 2.15%+$0.30 cards, 0%+$0.30 ACH (US).
pricingTiers: Each product has free micro-tier (e.g. Services 5 team members, Check-Ins 10/day, Giving 10 donations/mo) then usage-scaled paid tiers; People database free unlimited; Music Stand add-on $5/mo.
freeTier: YES: People free unlimited; every product has a free tier; Church Center base app free; 12-month free Giving for church plants.
trial: 30 days free on paid tiers, no fees; cancel/upgrade/downgrade anytime.
revenueEvidence: REVENUE NOT PUBLICLY DISCLOSED; Tracxn ESTIMATE ~$30.8M (secondary estimate, treat with caution).
customerEvidence: Church count NOT verified from primary sources reviewed; 100-250 employees; SOC 2 audited; Planning Center University training community.
growthEvidence: 20 years continuous growth (2006-2026); deliberate slow-bootstrapped pace per founders; 2024 Ministry Centered Foundation formed to stay 'not for sale.'
timeToLaunch: ~1 year of nights-and-weekends building inside church jobs before June 2006 launch.
validationMethod: Scratch-own-itch: solved their own Sunday-planning pain, then showed it at conferences and coded requested features same-day.
firstUserAcquisition: Saddleback Purpose Driven Worship Conference launch (June 2006) plus church visits; founder: 'showing people at conferences and visiting churches to help them get set up.'
first100Users: NOT PUBLICLY DISCLOSED; 'growing every week since' launch per 2018 founder interview.

secondaryDistribution: Content/SEO (blog, help center, Planning Center University), comparison pages, free-tier-led adoption, Church Center app network effects.

xStrategy: Social accounts exist (@planningcenter); no X-led growth evidence found.
productHuntStrategy: No notable Product Hunt launch found.
directOutreach: Early in-person church visits/setups (2006); no scaled outbound evidence.
partnerships: Integrations directory; Ministry Centered Foundation (2024) cements independence; no investors by design.
referralViral: Church-to-church referrals; volunteers carry product knowledge between churches; free Church Center app spreads congregant-side.
techStack: NOT VERIFIED from primary sources in this pass (commonly described as Rails monolith plus native mobile apps; treated as UNVERIFIED).
infrastructure: NOT PUBLICLY DISCLOSED; SOC 2 audited SaaS; status page and developer API published.
aiUsage: PicoLabs AI experiments plus 'AI tools you control' in product (2026); no AI at founding.
devMethod: Bootstrapped, ship-fast cadence ('ship fast, serve well'); one feature at a time; deliberate slow hiring.
soloFeasibility: POSSIBLY for single-module MVP (Services-like planner); full 8-product suite is a team job.
differentiation: Modular buy-only-what-you-need pricing with genuinely free tiers; founder-owned independence pledge; beloved service-planning UX.
competitiveMoat: MEDIUM: brand trust + data/workflow lock-in + independence narrative; modules individually replaceable.
competitors: Breeze/Tithely, ChurchTrac, Pushpay, Subsplash, Planning Center clones, Realm/ACS, ChurchSuite.
competitiveWeaknesses: Modular pricing stacks up for mid-size churches ($100-$600+/mo per ChurchTrac comparison); no accounting module (needs QuickBooks); steeper setup than all-in-ones.
legalPrivacy: SOC 2 audited; GDPR content published 2018; nonprofit/church data sensitivity.
zeroUpfront: YES (prototype: single service-planning module buildable with free tooling; distribution via own church network)
mrr100: HIGH ($100 MRR ≈ 2-4 small churches on paid modules)
learn: Scratch-own-itch plus founder-led conference selling can compound for 20 years without sales staff; free tiers per module beat freemium suite.
notCopy: Do not copy 8-module scope at launch; start with one beloved workflow (Services) and expand only on demand.

competitiveWeaknesses: Micro-team (3) vs funded rivals; no visible distribution engine; brand subsumed — the cautionary outcome itself.
legalPrivacy: Church donor/PII data; Tithely legal/privacy umbrella now applies.
mrr100: UNKNOWN (pricing dated/unverified; $3/user/mo quote would imply ~34 users — treat as UNRELIABLE)
learn: A good bootstrapped product without a distribution engine becomes an acqui-merge: Elvanto's tech survived inside Tithe.ly, its independence did not.
notCopy: Do not enter a crowded vertical with product parity but no distribution edge; decide early whether you are building to lead, to niche, or to merge.
primaryEvidence: PR Newswire Nov 14 2018 Tithe.ly–Elvanto merger release (8,500 churches/45 countries, 3-year process, Sinclair role); elvanto.com (current 'a Tithe.ly company' status, feature/API surface); Tracxn (founded 2010, unfunded, 3 staff, $3/user/mo quote); PitchBook (acquired Nov 2018 by Tithe.ly). No founder interviews or revenue records found — the UNKNOWN-heavy honesty case.
